verdicts.note: Not a lone ESSB 6346 vote: yes on 6346 final passage [S11], yes on ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5813 in 2025 [S22][S24] (pole_b), against yes on eight failed narrowing/tax-cut amendments [S14]-[S21] and on I-2111 in 2024 [S26] (pole_a). All checked against the cached roll calls. Several independent recorded votes justify high; the mix justifies +1 rather than +2.

Negative (strengthen current system) is the better reading, but the evidence is local capacity (urgent care, clinics, training, St. Michael oversight [S5]), which says nothing about insurance-system design, and the campaign section is headed 'Affordable Healthcare for All'. Placing him on this axis is an inference from the absence of single-payer language; low.
Rests on reproductive-rights evidence only (constitutional amendment for the right to choose [S5]), as the narrowed social definition requires.
Mixed record verified: yea on I-2081 (2024) and named co-sponsor of HB 1296 plus yea on both House final-passage votes (2025). The later, more active action is pole_b, so +1 medium fits.
Not vote-based; independent sources are the 2026 KDN Q&A ('I will oppose new state income taxes' [S3]), campaign site [S2], pamphlet [S1] and the 2024 call to lower the gas tax [S5].
Not campaign-site-only: the population-plus-inflation budget cap appears in the KDN Q&A [S3] as well as the site [S2], with 'live within its means' in the pamphlet [S1].

Pole_a is clear (more officers, ease laws that 'hamstring' arrests, stand with law enforcement [S5][S2]), but in the same 2024 interview he acknowledged concerns over 'violations of people's rights' and proposed a citizen review board [S5], and his pamphlet lists 'real help and shelter for the mentally ill' [S1]. Not fully pole_a; -1.
Sources are the campaign site [S2], KDN 2026 Q&A [S3] and KDN 2024 [S5], not the site alone.
Unlike Ilgen (Pos 1), holds no party or public office; two unsuccessful runs do not reduce the outsider case.

Rests on Growth Management Act reform 'without one-size-fits-all Olympia rules' / 'without state mandates' on housing [S3][S2], which is legitimate local-control evidence. His school-governance positions are correctly kept on parental-rights and not used here.
